12 /-!
13 # Finite types
14 
15 This file defines a typeclass to state that a type is finite.
16 
17 ## Main declarations
18 
19 * `Fintype α`:  Typeclass saying that a type is finite. It takes as fields a `Finset` and a proof
20   that all terms of type `α` are in it.
21 * `Finset.univ`: The finset of all elements of a fintype.
22 
23 See `Data.Fintype.Basic` for elementary results,
24 `Data.Fintype.Card` for the cardinality of a fintype,
25 the equivalence with `Fin (Fintype.card α)`, and pigeonhole principles.
26 
27 ## Instances
28 
29 Instances for `Fintype` for
30 * `{x // p x}` are in this file as `Fintype.subtype`
31 * `Option α` are in `Data.Fintype.Option`
32 * `α × β` are in `Data.Fintype.Prod`
33 * `α ⊕ β` are in `Data.Fintype.Sum`
34 * `Σ (a : α), β a` are in `Data.Fintype.Sigma`
35 
36 These files also contain appropriate `Infinite` instances for these types.
37 
38 `Infinite` instances for `ℕ`, `ℤ`, `Multiset α`, and `List α` are in `Data.Fintype.Lattice`.
39 -/

51 variable {α β γ : Type*}
52 
53 /-- `Fintype α` means that `α` is finite, i.e. there are only
54   finitely many distinct elements of type `α`. The evidence of this
55   is a finset `elems` (a list up to permutation without duplicates),
56   together with a proof that everything of type `α` is in the list. -/
57 class Fintype (α : Type*) where
58   /-- The `Finset` containing all elements of a `Fintype` -/
59   elems : Finset α
60   /-- A proof that `elems` contains every element of the type -/
61   complete : ∀ x : α, x ∈ elems
62 
63 /-! ### Preparatory lemmas -/

67 theorem nodup_map_iff_injOn {f : α → β} {s : Finset α} :
68     (Multiset.map f s.val).Nodup ↔ Set.InjOn f s := by
69   simp [Multiset.nodup_map_iff_inj_on s.nodup, Set.InjOn]
70 
71 end Finset

75 variable [DecidableEq α] {a : α} {f : α → β} {s : Finset α} {t : Set β} {t' : Finset β}
76 
77 instance [DecidableEq β] : Decidable (Set.InjOn f s) :=
78   -- Use custom implementation for better performance.
79   decidable_of_iff ((Multiset.map f s.val).Nodup) Finset.nodup_map_iff_injOn

81 instance [DecidableEq β] : Decidable (Set.BijOn f s t') :=
82   inferInstanceAs (Decidable (_ ∧ _ ∧ _))

86 namespace Finset
87 
88 variable [Fintype α] {s t : Finset α}
89 
90 /-- `univ` is the universal finite set of type `Finset α` implied from
91   the assumption `Fintype α`. -/
92 def univ : Finset α :=
93   @Fintype.elems α _
94 
95 @[simp, grind ←]
96 theorem mem_univ (x : α) : x ∈ (univ : Finset α) :=
97   Fintype.complete x
98 
99 theorem mem_univ_val : ∀ x, x ∈ (univ : Finset α).1 := by simp
100 
101 theorem eq_univ_iff_forall : s = univ ↔ ∀ x, x ∈ s := by simp [Finset.ext_iff]
102 
103 theorem eq_univ_of_forall : (∀ x, x ∈ s) → s = univ :=
104   eq_univ_iff_forall.2
105 
106 @[simp, norm_cast]
107 theorem coe_univ : ↑(univ : Finset α) = (Set.univ : Set α) := by ext; simp
108 
109 @[simp, norm_cast]
110 theorem coe_eq_univ : (s : Set α) = Set.univ ↔ s = univ := by rw [← coe_univ, coe_inj]
111 
112 @[simp]
113 theorem subset_univ (s : Finset α) : s ⊆ univ := fun a _ => mem_univ a
114 
115 theorem mem_filter_univ {p : α → Prop} [DecidablePred p] : ∀ x, x ∈ univ.filter p ↔ p x := by simp
116 
117 end Finset

119 namespace Mathlib.Meta
120 open Lean Elab Term Meta Batteries.ExtendedBinder Parser.Term PrettyPrinter.Delaborator SubExpr
121 
122 /-- Elaborate set builder notation for `Finset`.
123 
124 * `{x | p x}` is elaborated as `Finset.filter (fun x ↦ p x) Finset.univ` if the expected type is
125   `Finset ?α`.
126 * `{x : α | p x}` is elaborated as `Finset.filter (fun x : α ↦ p x) Finset.univ` if the expected
127   type is `Finset ?α`.
128 * `{x ∉ s | p x}` is elaborated as `Finset.filter (fun x ↦ p x) sᶜ` if either the expected type is
129   `Finset ?α` or the expected type is not `Set ?α` and `s` has expected type `Finset ?α`.
130 * `{x ≠ a | p x}` is elaborated as `Finset.filter (fun x ↦ p x) {a}ᶜ` if the expected type is
131   `Finset ?α`.
132 
133 See also
134 * `Data.Set.Defs` for the `Set` builder notation elaborator that this elaborator partly overrides.
135 * `Data.Finset.Basic` for the `Finset` builder notation elaborator partly overriding this one for
136   syntax of the form `{x ∈ s | p x}`.
137 * `Data.Fintype.Basic` for the `Finset` builder notation elaborator handling syntax of the form
138   `{x | p x}`, `{x : α | p x}`, `{x ∉ s | p x}`, `{x ≠ a | p x}`.
139 * `Order.LocallyFinite.Basic` for the `Finset` builder notation elaborator handling syntax of the
140   form `{x ≤ a | p x}`, `{x ≥ a | p x}`, `{x < a | p x}`, `{x > a | p x}`.
141 -/
142 @[term_elab setBuilder]
143 meta def elabFinsetBuilderSetOf : TermElab
144   | `({ $x:ident | $p }), expectedType? => do
145     -- If the expected type is not known to be `Finset ?α`, give up.
146     unless ← knownToBeFinsetNotSet expectedType? do throwUnsupportedSyntax
147     elabTerm (← `(Finset.filter (fun $x:ident ↦ $p) Finset.univ)) expectedType?
148   | `({ $x:ident : $t | $p }), expectedType? => do
149     -- If the expected type is not known to be `Finset ?α`, give up.
150     unless ← knownToBeFinsetNotSet expectedType? do throwUnsupportedSyntax
151     elabTerm (← `(Finset.filter (fun $x:ident : $t ↦ $p) Finset.univ)) expectedType?
152   | `({ $x:ident ∉ $s:term | $p }), expectedType? => do
153     -- If the expected type is known to be `Set ?α`, give up. If it is not known to be `Set ?α` or
154     -- `Finset ?α`, check the expected type of `s`.
155     unless ← knownToBeFinsetNotSet expectedType? do
156       let ty ← try whnfR (← inferType (← elabTerm s none)) catch _ => throwUnsupportedSyntax
157       -- If the expected type of `s` is not known to be `Finset ?α`, give up.
158       match_expr ty with
159       | Finset _ => pure ()
160       | _ => throwUnsupportedSyntax
161     -- Finally, we can elaborate the syntax as a finset.
162     -- TODO: Seems a bit wasteful to have computed the expected type but still use `expectedType?`.
163     elabTerm (← `(Finset.filter (fun $x:ident ↦ $p) $sᶜ)) expectedType?
164   | `({ $x:ident ≠ $a | $p }), expectedType? => do
165     -- If the expected type is not known to be `Finset ?α`, give up.
166     unless ← knownToBeFinsetNotSet expectedType? do throwUnsupportedSyntax
167     elabTerm (← `(Finset.filter (fun $x:ident ↦ $p) (singleton $a)ᶜ)) expectedType?
168   | _, _ => throwUnsupportedSyntax
169 
170 /-- Delaborator for `Finset.filter`. The `pp.funBinderTypes` option controls whether
171 to show the domain type when the filter is over `Finset.univ`. -/
172 @[app_delab Finset.filter] meta def delabFinsetFilter : Delab :=
173   whenPPOption getPPNotation do
174   let #[_, p, _, t] := (← getExpr).getAppArgs | failure
175   guard p.isLambda
176   let i ← withNaryArg 1 <| withBindingBodyUnusedName (pure ⟨·⟩)
177   let p ← withNaryArg 1 <| withBindingBody i.getId delab
178   if t.isAppOfArity ``Finset.univ 2 then
179     if ← getPPOption getPPFunBinderTypes then
180       let ty ← withNaryArg 0 delab
181       `({$i:ident : $ty | $p})
182     else
183       `({$i:ident | $p})
184   -- check if `t` is of the form `s₀ᶜ`, in which case we display `x ∉ s₀` instead
185   else if t.isAppOfArity ``Compl.compl 3 then
186     let #[_, _, s₀] := t.getAppArgs | failure
187     -- if `s₀` is a singleton, we can even use the notation `x ≠ a`
188     if s₀.isAppOfArity ``Singleton.singleton 4 then
189       let t ← withNaryArg 3 <| withNaryArg 2 <| withNaryArg 3 delab
190       `({$i:ident ≠ $t | $p})
191     else
192       let t ← withNaryArg 3 <| withNaryArg 2 delab
193       `({$i:ident ∉ $t | $p})
194   else
195     let t ← withNaryArg 3 delab
196     `({$i:ident ∈ $t | $p})
197 
198 end Mathlib.Meta

204 instance decidablePiFintype {α} {β : α → Type*} [∀ a, DecidableEq (β a)] [Fintype α] :
205     DecidableEq (∀ a, β a) := fun f g =>
206   decidable_of_iff (∀ a ∈ @univ α _, f a = g a)
207     (by simp [funext_iff])
208 
209 instance decidableForallFintype {p : α → Prop} [DecidablePred p] [Fintype α] :
210     Decidable (∀ a, p a) :=
211   decidable_of_iff (∀ a ∈ @univ α _, p a) (by simp)
212 
213 instance decidableExistsFintype {p : α → Prop} [DecidablePred p] [Fintype α] :
214     Decidable (∃ a, p a) :=
215   decidable_of_iff (∃ a ∈ @univ α _, p a) (by simp)
216 
217 instance decidableMemRangeFintype [Fintype α] [DecidableEq β] (f : α → β) :
218     DecidablePred (· ∈ Set.range f) := fun _ => Fintype.decidableExistsFintype
219 
220 instance decidableSubsingleton [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {s : Set α} [DecidablePred (· ∈ s)] :
221     Decidable s.Subsingleton := decidable_of_iff (∀ a ∈ s, ∀ b ∈ s, a = b) Iff.rfl
222

226   decidable_of_iff (a.1 = b.1) Equiv.coe_fn_injective.eq_iff

233 theorem nodup_map_univ_iff_injective [Fintype α] {f : α → β} :
234     (Multiset.map f univ.val).Nodup ↔ Function.Injective f := by
235   rw [nodup_map_iff_injOn, coe_univ, Set.injOn_univ]
236 
237 instance decidableInjectiveFintype [DecidableEq β] [Fintype α] :
238     DecidablePred (Injective : (α → β) → Prop) :=
239   -- Use custom implementation for better performance.
240   fun f => decidable_of_iff ((Multiset.map f univ.val).Nodup) nodup_map_univ_iff_injective
241 
242 instance decidableSurjectiveFintype [DecidableEq β] [Fintype α] [Fintype β] :
243     DecidablePred (Surjective : (α → β) → Prop) :=
244   fun x ↦ inferInstanceAs <| Decidable (∀ b, ∃ a, x a = b)
245 
246 instance decidableBijectiveFintype [DecidableEq β] [Fintype α] [Fintype β] :
247     DecidablePred (Bijective : (α → β) → Prop) :=
248   fun x ↦ inferInstanceAs <| Decidable (Injective x ∧ Surjective x)
249 
250 instance decidableRightInverseFintype [DecidableEq α] [Fintype α] (f : α → β) (g : β → α) :
251     Decidable (Function.RightInverse f g) :=
252   inferInstanceAs <| Decidable (∀ x, g (f x) = x)
253 
254 instance decidableLeftInverseFintype [DecidableEq β] [Fintype β] (f : α → β) (g : β → α) :
255     Decidable (Function.LeftInverse f g) :=
256   inferInstanceAs <| Decidable (∀ x, f (g x) = x)

258 instance subsingleton (α : Type*) : Subsingleton (Fintype α) :=
259   ⟨fun ⟨s₁, h₁⟩ ⟨s₂, h₂⟩ => by congr; simp [Finset.ext_iff, h₁, h₂]⟩

263 -- adding `@[implicit_reducible]` causes downstream breakage
264 set_option warn.classDefReducibility false in
265 /-- Given a predicate that can be represented by a finset, the subtype
266 associated to the predicate is a fintype. -/
267 protected def subtype {p : α → Prop} (s : Finset α) (H : ∀ x : α, x ∈ s ↔ p x) :
268     Fintype { x // p x } :=
269   ⟨⟨s.1.pmap Subtype.mk fun x => (H x).1, s.nodup.pmap fun _ _ _ _ => congr_arg Subtype.val⟩,
270     fun ⟨x, px⟩ => Multiset.mem_pmap.2 ⟨x, (H x).2 px, rfl⟩⟩
271 
272 -- adding `@[implicit_reducible]` causes downstream breakage
273 set_option warn.classDefReducibility false in
274 /-- Construct a fintype from a finset with the same elements. -/
275 def ofFinset {p : Set α} (s : Finset α) (H : ∀ x, x ∈ s ↔ x ∈ p) : Fintype p :=
276   Fintype.subtype s H
277 
278 end Fintype
